newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Stg gears up for break of 2.7840 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Stg gears up for break of 2.7840 marks.

text.p: Sterling/mark looks to have formed a base on hourly charts and should probe higher during the European session, chart analysts said.

The pound took out initial resistance at 2.7750 marks in early trade and now faces sturdier barriers around 2.7800 and 2.7840 -- previous support breached on Friday, said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America in London.
"That's the level it has to recover now -- if it breaks above there we're looking for 2.79, then 2.7940 and 2.7980 which capped it for most of last week," Dunne said.
Violation of those levels will reopen 2.8200-8350, levels not seen since early May, chartists said.
The pound was quoted at 2.7762/72 marks at 0733 GMT, up from late Friday's European level of 2.7728/33.
Support cuts in around 2.7680 marks on hourly charts and then near overnight lows at 2.7635, technical analysts said.
Sterling also ticked higher against the dollar in early Europe, knocking on the door of resistance around $1.6390/6400. A break there is seen opening the way towards $1.65.
Friday's highs around $1.6425 will be the pound's first hurdle, ahead of previous peaks at $1.6460 and $1.6490.
On the downside, sterling must hold $1.6315, Friday's low, if it is to achieve higher levels today, chartists said.
A slip below there will take it back to old ranges with trendline support around $1.6240 and congestion around $1.6170-60, which propped the pound during its recent consolidation phase.
Sterling was trading at $1.6390/00 at 0742 GMT versus $1.6377/82 in late Europe on Friday.
